title: Start with a feeling: How to define your first video game
summary: Before you list features, name the feeling. Learn how to define what your video game is about with one sentence and three design pillars – no coding needed.
body_markdown:
## **Write one sentence, then three pillars**


Now combine your feeling and your fantasy into a single experience statement:


*My game makes the player feel \[feeling\] by letting them be \[role\] who \[core action\].*


For example: “My game makes the player feel calm and needed by letting them be a lighthouse keeper who guides lost ships home.”


Next, break that sentence into design pillars – short rules that describe the experience your game has to deliver. Most guides suggest[three or four](https://generalistprogrammer.com/tutorials/game-design-pillars-explained) . With fewer, they’re too broad to rule anything out. With more, almost any idea fits one of them. Good pillars name feelings or rules, not features or genres.


For the lighthouse game example, they might be:


- No rush, ever.
- Small acts of care matter.
- The coast remembers you.


Indie team Saltstone Studios used pillars to shape its first game, *The Pale Beyond* . One of them, Every Decision Has a Face, meant players always saw the character a choice would affect – which went on to shape the game’s systems and character design.[The team calls its pillars](https://saltstonestudios.com/2025/12/08/game-design-pillars/) “probably the main reason our first game was any good at all.”
